question: Does increasing the raw RGBA IPC response chunk size improve the production image preparation deadline result for the pinned synthetic fixture?

control.deadlineStart: Immediately before each ImagePreparationService.prepare call; this is later than the product selection start.
control.instrumentation: Diagnostic timing sink and worker stage timing were disabled. Each sample used a fresh ImagePreparationService and real Electron utilityProcess; the next sample waited for the prior worker to exit.

interpretation: The 2 MiB run had the same success count as the latest 1 MiB repeat and a 26.42 ms higher median; the 4 MiB run had one timeout and a 154.30 ms higher median than that repeat. These sequential five-sample observations do not establish that chunk size caused the timing differences.
Every successful candidate sample matched the pinned full-frame RGBA SHA-256. The 4 MiB timeout observed request abort and worker exit.
Expected chunk counts and tail sizes are arithmetic from 64,000,000 output bytes and the candidate source constant; this runner did not record actual per-message chunk telemetry or RSS.
The runner asserts worker exit was observed, but does not assert the exit code. Recorded exit codes were zero.
The 3,000 ms budget starts immediately before service.prepare, not at the full product selection start, so these measurements do not close the product deadline gate.
decision: Keep the production default at 1 MiB. Do not adopt either larger candidate from this timing-only comparison; chunk-count, memory, ASAR transport, and fuller selection-start deadline evidence remain open.
